Tales of Maj'Eyal is one of the bigger Roguelikes that along with Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup and Dwarf Fortress help set the standards for what makes a good Roguelike.
Unlike the two other roguelikes listed above you'll find an actual story being played out along with Lore and Monster Details that really tell you about the world your character is playing in; while not getting in the way of in-game play. Game Mechanics are plentiful but they are spelled out and not hidden from the player. User Interface for the most part is easy to get into and use.
There are a couple of hurdles one will need to commit to however in order to play this game - like any Roguelike there is the overall Game Depth and Learning Curve and Tales of Maj'Eyal is no different. Character skills sort of level up similar to what you might find in an MMORPG or Diablo-like, but skills themselves are also much like their counterparts - not descriptive enough to tell you what they do and requiring you have to test them out or read up on them.
For people coming from other Roguelikes, you may be thrown off by the sheer Tactical Nature of combat, Additionally it is worth noting that the game is meant to be played in Adventurer Mode - IE, Multiple Lives, not One. Lastly, the game is long - very long. A full run in the original Age of Ascendancy Campaign (The Main Vanilla Campaign that the game started with) from start to actual finish is probably going to be longer then most other Roguelikes bar a few.
All in all though, this is a very enjoyable game. Once you get past the couple tidbits that might hold you back or throw you off you'll likely have lots of fun playing with multiple races and classes in separate but distinct ways.

This is a great roguelike. It is more accessible to inexperienced players than most roguelikes. It has several difficulty settings, and characters can gain extra lives as they gain experience. In addition, you can always reallocate the last four talent points you have spent. As a result, players can be successful by experimenting in-game rather than finding the optimal build online.
That's not to say the game is not difficult. Expect to die many times before winning. However, there are so many races and classes to try that the game never feels stale. Tired of going toe-to-toe with swarms of monsters as a sword-and-shield wielding Bulwark? Try altering the flow of time as a Paradox mage. A large number of classes, races, and talent categories are available to be unlocked as you play as well. Your character sheets will be uploaded to
if you are logged in in-game, and you can search the repository for other players' characters. This is a great way to get some idea of how to play a class well if you don't want to go in completely blind.
Classes aren't particularly well-balanced, but you can be successful with any of them with enough experience playing. The difficulty can also feel a rather inconsistent throughout the game. Most enemies will be trivial to defeat, but then you might be rapidly taken down by a rare monster in a couple turns. Despite some short-comings, this is still an excellent game. If you're not convinced it is worth buying on Steam, it is available for free from the developer's web site minus some donator benefits and the convenience of being on Steam. The game is actively being worked on; I can't wait to see what new features and abilities are introduced in the future.

Tales of Maj'Eyal (TOME for short) is a in turn based roguelike that at first glance is something many would pass over but it comes with an amazing amount of character customization, story and enjoyable difficulty. This game also has, at the time of this review, the most achievements of any game on Steam. There is also an explorer mode which allows you to enjoy the story, up to Insanity mode to maximize the pain. The Steam edition also has a connected community chat in game which allows you to share death messages or interesting finds to talk about. The community is wonderful, the developers also update the game with new features. If you are still unsure about the game you can download the game for free at the developers website. If you like it, consider picking this up on Steam and supporting the developers!

Please note that this Review is reflecting my personal opinion on this game. I have also been reading other reviews and will go over how I feel about topics other reviews have touched on.
So I have been enjoying Raid a lot since its release 4 days ago and am in no way disapointed in how the game has turned out and is developing.
The game has been labled as the 'spiritual sucsessor' to the game Payday 2 that was also published by 'Starbreeze studios' but programmed and developed by 'Overkill' while at the current stage of the game I do not think it is as rich in content as Payday 2 is right now, but I still think that it has the potential to reach or even pass the sucsess Payday 2 has had, if the Developers do everything correctly.
A big thing I have noticed is the Developers have been extemly active in communicating with the playerbase of Raid, if its in the Steam forums, subreddit or discord they have been everywhere fixing issues and taking feedback. One thing I am extremly supprised by (as I have never seen another studio do it) is the weekly livestream the Devs are hosting,  it has a long Q&A section, information about new content and community polls about what new content should come first. While I am not sure if the Livestreams can countinue to be held weekly, until now they have been and I think its a great sign that the game is making big progress.
As for gameplay the game is mostly made out of you slaughtering nazi's while they storm at you (sometimes you will also encounter tanks and other special enemies), while the game does feature the possiblity of stealth in certain missions. Stealth is extremely hard to do, but possible if you think you are up for a challenge. The game has a rather limited amount of weapons as of now, but they have already announced 3 more comming soon, personally I don't feel that the limited amount is a bad thing, until now I've been fine playing with one weapon  and working on unlocking all upgrades for it (upgrades are unlocked by completing challenges such as 'kill 250 enemies that are 20 more meters away from you). The weapons feel balanced and have a very good/fitting ammo capacity.
Many have said that the graphics look horrible, I disagree. While the graphics can be better I think that in the stage they are now they are fully acceptable. The graphics also fit the atmosphere and time very well.
The Game runs of a class based system, there are 4 classes to chose from: Recon, Assault, Insurgent, or Demolition, you will need to create a different 'profile/character' for each class. That means you pick your class and then you pick one of the currently 4 characters. The profiles you create all run on their own level, so bringing all 4 classes to the current max (level 40) will be a very hard to do challenge. Each time you level up you can chose from 3 different upgrades (except for each 10th level, then you can only chose 1 upgrade) and the upgrades will make your character stronger. The devs did mention that they might add a non-character based leveling system.
The game runs very well with very fluent FPS, I've never encounterd any kind of 'lag-spike' and until now only 1 chrash that happend when I tried tabbing out of the game when I just completed a mission (that was the first and only time it had happend).
And the game featues a 'borderless-windowed' mode... thank you
TL;DR: The game is very fun (especially with friends). While there is room for improvement with the current rate of developement I am very certain that the Devs will make it even better as time goes on.

This game is very fun to play in my opinion. One thing I was excited for was seeing what kind of German troops they would throw at us, and in missions, they throw quite a bit of different germans at you. The enemies use their real german military unit names, which to me is gibrish and can't remember for the life of my but that helps make the game feel like that world war 2 theme that we all love. In the base game, there are 12 weapons(13 if you count the golden M1 Garand you got if you preordered, however there is a regular m1 garand for those who did not preorder), and 5 melee weapons.  Some of the most notably cool weapons in my opinion are the BAR, 1911, Garand, STG 44, MP38, MG42 and the Sterling SMG and mauser. Guns in the beta were very weak but they gave all around stat buffs to all of them for the full game which is nice. You have about 11 raids, which after playing about half of them, are really fun. Alongside that are operations which are chained raids that create a story and after completing the entire operation(takes a bit), nab you a big bundle of rewards(Lots of xp and whatnot). Lastly they also have "Outlaw" raids, and these raids are designed to prop up as file bundles in regular raids that when you grab, you now have access to an outlaw raid after your current mission is over. These were made to get the player a lot of loot that can be bagged and secured. These outlaw raids are not about damaging the nazi war machine, but instead benefitting your pockets with nazi gold, stolen paintings, etc.
Instead of skills like payday, you have proficiences which you can increase as you level up. You go down this line and at every level, they give you 3 skills, and you can only choose one. Once you chose that one, you wait until you level up again and then you can choose another 1 skill out of 3. Interesting system and it seems to work so that your character can get powerful and definitely get his stats boosted, but not a literally insane robot that mows down 500+ men in every mission lol.(you can probably still do that though if you have the time and patience, and a good gun)
Also, one more thing to note, the cutscenes in this game are hilarious. They use John Cleese as a British intelligence man and are so damn goofy. After the missions, they show this guy dressed up as hitler, getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off in multiple ways after a successful mission that you have completed. But if you fail, it shows him very happy and makes you feel like a dunce, lol. Well played LionGameLion, well played :P.
My total rating for this game: 9/10 I truly have fun when i boot this game up and hop into missions, they are not a walk in the park like payday but are doable and have a good challenge to them, making them a worthwhile experience. If you like payday, I think you will truly enjoy this game.

Assassin's Creed 2 actually changes quite alot from its predecessor. Instead of collecting information on your target because of the story, you assassinate your target as it is part of the story. And like last time, there is an amazing feeling about running away and hiding from countless gaurds on your tail right after a majestic assassination. Parkour in this is similar to the last with sweet Architecture to climb and run across, giving off a completely different vibe than the original. What's the best indicator that something is a sequel? Well the number 2 of course! Which is why you now have 2 hidden blades! Some combat animations are quite satisfying although i think its become quite easy and i still enjoy the slower paced clashes of the original with close ups of bringing down your enemies. Alright, this game is pretty good.
As of the first day of release, the game says I have 291.8 hours in the game. I bought it during the second day of beta, but even then I haven't put nearly that many hours into the game. Subtracting negligence of closing the game when I'm done, I've probably put around 20-50 hours into the game actually playing. All of it has been focused on a save with Zürich and I'm one season and a half in. (won the league first season tho!!!)
I've played enough to notice the big improvements and the big issues with Football Manager 2018.
The biggest improvement, in my opinion, is how the AI handles transfers. This may not seem like a big deal to people who don't tend to play 10 years into a save, but for me this is MASSIVE. In fm17, you'd see certain big teams just load up on players with crazy high current ability without ever trying to meet their team needs. It's just absurd when PSG has 6 world class wingers. Again, I haven't played a lot into the game and I've really only gone through one big transfer window, but I've already seen improvement. I had a player named Dwamena that just scorched defenses in the Swiss League, 36 goals in league play. His current ability at the time I sold him was 136 and he only has a potential ability of 146. Now, that's not too bad, but the price I sold him at to the teams that wanted him, it was clear that teams weren't just looking at numbers but instead form. I sold him for 24m to Monaco, with others team bidding just as much to get him in like: Dortmund, Napoli, and Juventus(!!!). Juventus is a BIG team, it doesn't make a lot of sense for them to bid 22m for a player with 136 Current Abiliy, but it does make sense for them to bid for a player that finished third in the european golden boot race. I just appreciate this a lot more, and I hope it adds some extra realism to long term saves.
Other improvmements include the new player roles, especially in the midfield. I love using the carrilero, as it offers good defensive play to my rapid attacking style football. The new dynamics system is mostly a plus, however the fragility of players can often call into question your will to live apparently. I haven't really run into this issue of having your entire team begging for you to step down, but I've seen it a good bit. This is especially problematic with teams like Ajax that have players constantly coming in and out. This can add a bit of frustration or challenge from how you look at it, but any issues I've had from players are easily dealt with if you have a good captain. The graphics engine does look better, but there's still a lot be desired. The regens (newgens) also don't look so wacky this year, this is IMPORTANT. I'm pretty sure the match engine has also changed a little, but besides one issue, it's just as good if not better than fm17. The new data reports you get from your analysts are also great, USE THEM they're so useful. And the injury tab is nice to look at every once in a while as well. ALSO!!! newgens can come out as gay!! While it is very rare, I will take my chances and try to build an all queer team to take over the world. I think that's my ultimate challenge for fm18.
Now lets get to some issues. The first thing I want to mention is from the match engine. I had two, absolutely AMAZING goals scored from my wingers... that were trying to cross from 40 yards out. Now that's some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It hasn't happened to me yet, but crosses almost becoming goals is a big issue this year. Hope SI addresses that a bit real quick. Regens (newgens) still seem to pop up balding at 16, which I get is a reality for some, but I don't think it happens at the same rate as fm thinks it does. The repetitive minigame of press conferences continues, which isn't really that much of an issue but if someone could mod and add like a couple extra thousand questions and reponses that'd make me v happy. These are just small complaints that aren't really even mostly original to fm18, but they all pale in comparison to what I think is the biggest issue with fm18.
The interface is hot garbage. I'm sorry SI, but this stuff is so counterintuitive. Is it bad enough to make the game impossible to play? Not at all, and the more I play the game the more I'm getting used to it and can easily just flow through the screens with ease like I did in fm17, but it's still a step-down from previous years. The interface, on the whole, looks pretty nice. It is indeed, an attractive interface! But... Using the interface just feels
During the game, the buttons for editing your tactic and making substitutions just aren't where they need to be. The button to confirm your changes is fairly small, and it's in the bottom right hand corner! When I first started, it took me a couple seconds to find it and it took me a couple hours to just get used to it being there. The scout reports you get aren't much different, but how they're delivered is terrible. If you scout a player, you no longer just get the individual scout report but instead it's bundled along with 30 players your scouts recommend and whatever players agents are throwing around trying to get signed. Viewing the scout report from that still feels like a hassle. The scouting page also just looks a lot less clean. There are positives and negatives to this, first you get more information. That's generally good, but the information doesn't aid you too much in your process of finding the players you want, that's the issue. The negatives is that it just hurts your eyes to scroll through it all, it's just so much! In fm17, it'd be a nice little bar with whatever data you wanted but mostly their name, position, and goals/assists/whatever stats you like. It was nice, easy. The green used EVERYWHERE in the interface is especially annoying however. It's not refreshing to look at, and just isn't as easy on the eyes as a nice lucid grey may be. I'm sure there are other interface issues I can't remember, but these are the first ones that come to mind.
The good thing about the interface is that I think it can largely be skinned. Now that skinners have access to the base skins to edit, I'm eagerly awaiting to see what we get a couple weeks from now.
Although I think the interface is worse than last years, it still wouldn't be enough for me to say I don't recommend getting this game. If you really enjoy playing football manager every year, you're going to enjoy this years version. The new roles offer up some more creativity for your midfield and the AI decision making just feels so much better this year. If you're a bit skeptical and think the improvements aren't worth $50.00, then that's fair. But if you can catch this game on sale, I'd snatch at it.

Still, while highly annoying, it doesn't detract from the overall package.  It's worth a play.

Think of this game as Metal Slug, but MUCH deeper.  It's got a quest system with goals for every mission you do, including secret goals.  You've got an absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of things to buy to upgrade your character.  You've got multiple different parts for your gun to interchange.  Stuff like a barrel, magazine, stock, etc.  You can have anything from a lightning sniper rifle to a fire submachine gun and everything in between, even being able to tweak how many bullets and your overall damage.  You've got a knife that you can also have many different versions of.  Useable items like first-aid kits, grenades, c4 to open some doors.
If you're a person who wants to get everything, buckle up.  It's going to take you an awful long time to afford everything.  Every mission is timed, which is a bit annoying at first.  Especially when you haven't had a chance to familiarize yourself with a particular map.  It's probably the biggest drawback to the game if you don't like being rushed.  You'll normally have plenty of time, but some missions don't give you much room to breathe.
Luckily, there's co-op to help you through some of the tougher missions.  You and up to 3 other people can join in the fun.  Tons of bosses, tons of quests, tons of guns.  It's how Metal Slug should've been designed in the first place.

This game is utterly difficult and you will die a lot. Of course that doesn't mean this is a bad game; in fact, the fact that it's so difficult is great because I was waiting for another challenging game which is fun to play. This game exceeded my expectations in every way.
The art style is so unique that you can apply a grayscale filter and it will look just like an old Disney cartoon. The fluidity of the controls (though I had to adjust the controls to fit me because the original gamepad controls weren't the best) were good (I played this game with a gamepad and highly recommend you do too). The difficulty is something else.... You can complete each level in "simple" mode which grants you access to the next area however in order to complete the game and meet the final boss you need to have beaten every level in "regular" mode which is quite difficult. That's something I found really nice since you might've bought an upgrade but you needed a different upgrade for a level, but how can you get more coins if you already beat all the levels in this game which give you coins? Beat the boss in simple mode which is considerably easier than regular which means you are able to move on and come back to that level later.
However, as much as I love this game... there are two things which need to be addressed. The game has a lot of RNG moments where you can either get very lucky or very unlucky; some bosses have an "RNG phase" which means that you might get one phase in this attempt but a different phase in the next attempt - which is okay, don't get me wrong - but the game doesn't balance the difficulty of those RNG phases correctly. Some phases are considerably more difficult than others. The other thing which needs to be addressed is that you can get hit outside the screen. This is a problem; a big problem especially in one boss fight where you're in a tower with a bee. You're supposed to jump on platforms but the platforms spawn outside of the screen (which is okay) but some projectiles which fly out of the screen can still hit you making it unfair (which is not okay). Fortunately those problems are mostly level specific and don't happen too often.
+ Unique art style
+ Smooth and fluid controls (gamepad recommended)
+ Difficult but possible
+ Fun to play
+ Amazing soundtrack
+ (Also no greedy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t)
- Some "RNG phases" / RNG moments
- Can sometimes be killed outside the screen but I have only experienced this in one level

When I first saw Cuphead a few years ago, I think I was drawn in by what many other people were drawn in by: the art style, including the visuals and the audio. The drawings of the game seemed like something very unique in video games, especially with the amount of work that was clearly required to create it. And some early trailers had some funny music going along, which made me really interested in how this game would turn out.
I was trying to keep watch on the game for a long while, but was very on-the-fence about it. In the best scenario, I was hoping for the game to simply be fun and for the art to not be the only successful point. As it turns out, the release of Cuphead drastically exceeded that "best scenario" for me.
The art in the game was well done down to the little tiny pieces. The music and sound effects all form an interesting perspective that fits with the visual style. The gameplay itself goes along with the cartoons and creates an intense, yet extremely fun, game. And that further recalls video games from just a couple of decades ago, with modern games usually being in a very different basket of experience.
Everything coalesces together almost perfectly for me, conquering any worries I had about this game over the years during its production.
Literally the biggest complaint against the game from the majority of players is that "It's too hard." Yet there is a large amount of people who have completed the game, and the overall reviews are surely up, up, and away into the positives for Cuphead.
While the game is indeed far from easy, and might get you frustrated, I think part of the experience is simply to not let your emotions overwhelm you. This applies to many video games and heck, many day-to-day experiences in life as a whole. The more angry and annoyed you get by the game, it's very likely you will do worse in completing the levels, and it compounds more anger into a vicious cycle.
If you take a step back and observe the levels and bosses, making notice of the patterns they use, you can definitely make your way through the game. If you are having an obscene amount of trouble with a certain boss, I would even say to take it one step at a time: focus on one particular attack and learn how to dodge it. Then move onto the next. Then eventually, you need to step up and move a little faster to get past multiple in a row. It is all really building a memory and learning how to tackle a "puzzle" in a way.
Cuphead is one of my favorite games of 2017 by far. Such a great experience.

If there's one way I'd sum up this game, it'd be "Hotline Miami: The Western", as it follows the same "Top-down shooter with some stealth elements where everyone dies in one hit" formula.
Story:
There's not much of an overarching plot to the game. An escaped Mexican slave with amnesia wanders into Texas and just kind of bumbles around, learning bits and pieces about his past and making enemies out of anyone and everyone due to his violent, abrasive personality. This is one of those grimdark stories where no one is truly sympathetic. Everyone is a violent, racist ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the protagonist included, and it's hard to even root for the protagonist when all of his problems are his own doing and he doesn't show even the slightest bit of remorse for his more heinous actions. I don't want to spoil too much about the ending, but it's somehow simultaneously disappointing yet appropriate. Everybody gets exactly what they deserve, but it's hard to feel any satisfaction from it.
Graphics:
The graphics are both a blessing and a curse. From a purely aesthetic standpoint they look great, and perfectly capture the gritty ugliness of the setting, and the black-and-white-with-the-occasional-bit-of-red look helps it stand out. Unfortunately, one thing that DOESN'T stand out are enemies. Since everything is in black and white, characters have an annoying tendency to blend into the background, which is absolutely insufferable when these characters are going to start shooting at you as soon as they see you.
Gameplay:
This game suffers from one of the biggest complaints I've seen about Hotline Miami 2: A large number of wide-open areas, in a game who's top-down nature and one-hit-kill status of every character is a terrible idea. Enemies often open fire on you before you can even see them, often leading to scenarios where you have to VERY CAREFULLY inch along, using the long range button to snoop around just ahead of you. Combined with the aforementioned problems with the art style, this can make some areas (such as the train levels) pure torture.
This game has a unique method of using guns, and I'm not entirely sure whether it's a good or bad thing. Two of the types of guns you'll be using are revolvers and bolt-action rifles, and instead of just pointing and shooting you have to♥♥♥♥♥♥the hammer on a revolver by holding down the right mouse button before you can shoot, and in-between each round fired from a rifle you have to click the right mouse button to prep the next round. There are also double-barreled shotguns, which can be fired twice in rapid succession but requires reloading immediately afterwards, and bows and arrows, which can simply be fired by holding down the left mouse button to nock an arrow and firing, but has a very low rate of fire compared to the guns. While this does add an extra wrinkle to combat, during more heated battles it can get tricky to fall into the left and right mouse button pattern required to fire off multiple rounds in succession. The ammo system also requires you to eject all the rounds from a gun before you drop it (otherwise those bullets go with the gun and end up wasted) and building up a supply of ammo requires you to stop in-between confrontations to grab every gun in sight and empty them out, which can get needlessly time-consuming at times.
tl;dr This is one of those games where I really wish Steam had an individual "Mixed" review option. Ultimately I think the good manages to edge out the bad and it's something you might want to pick up if it's on sale.

I want to recommend this game, but controls are such that I just can't.
I played initially with the keyboard, but found it clunky and not suited to the fast-paced nature of the game. I then played with the controller and found it even worse. To knife someone and then shoot their partner, for example, you need to press b to choose the knife, use the right trigger to stab them, press b to sheathe the knife, press the left trigger to♥♥♥♥♥♥your gun, then press the right trigger to shoot, all in the 0.5 seconds it takes for his partner to turn around.
The game gives you the illusion of choice, but very often there's only one correct way to win clear. You can't sneak because of the positioning of enemies, and you can't quietly stab them because as soon as someone notices you you are somehow incapable. You can't pick them off one at a time, because a single gunshot will prompt the entire cast to run at you. This would be less of a problem if you could quickly pick up ammunition, but you need to be in the exact spot and you need to stop for half a second... which is half a second too long, when you've got a chamber of six, and twelve enemies charging. I guess 12 *is* better than 6, but in this case that's a shame.
It's also missing simple things like custom resolutions, which is an absolute pain. Choose hi-res mode and you're limited to a 1920x1080 full screen, or a 1920x1080 window. Choose lo-res, and it's exactly the same. Really? You can't even make room for the taskbar? Or pressing 'a' to continue. You've got to use the right trigger or right bumper.
Otherwise, it is fun, and it is stylish, and with better controls I could really see myself enjoying it.

A nice tower defence game. It doesn't differ too much from other TD games, but it's pretty fun once you get a hang of it. Most of the standard mechanics associated with TD genre are here: a good tower variety, a good enemy variety, rock-paper-scissors tactic of using the right tower against the right enemy, scoreboards, and so on.
Graphically the game is very beautiful. Though at times I wished the towers looked a bit more different to one another, otherwise it can get confusing what is what. I do like the whole colour scheme of green towers being basic, yellow advanced, and red the best. The musical side of things could've been a bit better though. Most levels have between 20-30 waves, and can take a while to play through, so it would've been nice to have it spiced up with more memorable tunes. The A.I. narrator most times provides a nice commentary and keeps you entertained with his colourful personality, though at times he can be annoying when he keeps telling you about cores being stolen. *shakes fist*
Most levels had a very interesting design and forced you to think hard on how to channel enemies down a longer path and where would be the points of highest offense. They provided a nice challenge. A few felt like difficulty spikes and seemed unnecessarily convoluted (looking at you, Waste Disposal), but most were a great fun.
There were a few aspects that annoyed me slightly, so might be worth mentioning them. First one which I noticed straight away was how much punishment the enemies could sustain before going down. Even the weakest, most basic enemies could absorb a fair amount of damage, which in turn made many towers feel too weak. And this brings me to another one. Majority of towers are very situational and tend to have a lot more shortcomings than strengths. The only tower that I felt was all-round good at just about everything was the Cannon tower, and these usually formed the meat and potatoes of my defence, with all the other towers just acting in supporting roles. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but it means there is a bit too little room for experimentation with various setups.
Aside from the story mode, each map also has a variety of other modes, most providing some form of a new challenge, like enemies being tougher, or the cores which you must protect not going back to their starting location, and so on. So there's a lot of stuff to try out here and the completionists can easily sink tens or hundreds of hours in this game.
Overall, it's a fun TD game. Don't expect anything new and extraordinary, but if you like the genre, then you should definitely grab this game.

Dominate the world under a fascist banner, spread communism to the workers of the world, maintain the status quo of the democracies, or watch from the sidelines as the world goes up in flames. Either way, have fun doing it!

I feel as though i've played enough Hearts of Iron IV to recommend it to others, so here i am.
Firstly, i don't play a lot of grand strategy games, nor do i play many strategy games at all. However i'm rather fond of them when i have the time and Hearts of Iron certainly has captured my time.
Playing as all the different countries is amazing, and the constant viewing of a world map (albeit a few years out of date) has improved my map of country knowledge ten-fold. I've learnt much world war 2 history through hearts of iron and it's mods and have especially enjoyed the history (and subsequent playing) as China with the two dragons mod.
I have also had the pleasure of multiplayer hearts of iron, like civilisation it requires that all players have the same mods, but hearts of iron's multiplayer is generally more co-operative and easier to use in comparison to civilisation's multiplayer.
My only gripes with the game are the horrible content for money ratio when it comes to the colonel and field marshel editions of the game. While knowing that you will have access to the first two expansions is peace of mind if you plan on playing hearts of iron long-term, i don't think it's worth the  £67.99 upfront, and without any option to upgrade from one edition to another, it doesn't seem worth it -especially if you may not play it for too long.
My second gripe is the AI, it's not that great. I don't see much of a difference between easy and veteran difficulties and would have generally hopes the AI would have some strategy when not on land. The AI has trouble launching naval invasions or parachute invasions. Which means that (until the player gets involved) the war will never end, as neither the allies nor the axis have the potential to invade England/Japan respectively.
Overall though, a solid 8/10 even if you perhaps aren't too keen on the genre, it certainly gives you talking points for future conversations and can lead you into other world war two hobbies.

Pay no mind to the bethesda badge on the box, this is actually an id software game (and it IS in face developed by them). So straight out the door you should immediately remove fallout from your mind, and while you're at it borderlands (although the world is similar). Look at the games id made: Doom, Wolfenstein, and Quake are the ones that come to most minds and should be a great example of what kind of game this is
No, there is no real RPG element to this game. No there is no crazy loot system. No it is not a huge open world (although it is probably the most open world-ish of any id game). No it is not a multithreaded complex story. But then again, did any of id's games have any of that? So please stop thinking it's a bethesda game before you buy it, you'll thank me.
So what IS this game then? It's an id game. For its time it had amazing ground breaking graphics (and still looks great to this day). It has very tight and crisp combat with very well done controls, perfect level design, and amazing ai. And when I say amazing ai i mean I put it in my list of games with best ai. It's not mind blowing because of it's complexity and intuition, but because of the variety and character it gives all the enemies.
So what's the downside? This game is one of those games where a developer obviously is trying something new to the point where you feel it isn't in their typical style. As a result a lot of the "fluff" content and features feel not only mediocre, but also unnecessary. Also because this game does not focus primarily on level design it's not something I see myself going back and playing again and again like I would with the old doom and quake titles.
In short I do consider this a great game, but certainly not id's best form. The combat and level design are really at the quality only id was capable of (I say was because id is no longer id), and the new tech that Carmake put in this is pretty awesome. It's a blast and, while short lived overall, it is well worth every penny of the $10 price. It might even make you feel hopeful about the game industry again, you jaded ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

OK Let's start with the warning.
FOR ALL OF YOU PEOPLE LOOKING FOR AN EASY GAME TO COMPLETE: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!
Sanctum is HARD! You can't go in with a mentality of, "oh it's just a shooter, Ill just blast everything away!" or "oh it's just a tower defence, I'll just upgrade my towers" No, you must enter Sanctum with the mentality of," Ok, Ill start a small maze with lazers on top to defend agains air and ground, and near the end I'll wait and snipe the bobbleheads as they come." YES This game requires planning! So if you want a mindless shooter, look elsewhere. For all of you people who want to just try to upgrade your towers, you must realize that some creatures are going to be missed and head strait for your core ( the place you are defending ). Creatures like bobbleheads are only damaged in certain spots, and will not be killed easily by towers. YOU have to kill these guys, and soakers, I can't forget those damage loving guys.
YOUR WEAPONS!
All of the weapons are fun and easy to use! They all overheat/ need to be reloaded after constant use. The more you upgrade them the more ammo/coolant you have so upgrade them as much as possible.
They are your rudimentary assult rifle, sniper, rocket launcher, and freeze ray (pardon me if I missed some)
Wait, freeze rays aren't rudimentary!
And you have towers which act as elevators, walls, lazers, lightning bolts, and more, and every tower can be upgraded, (except for the elevator because I mean really... :P) Each tower targets the air, the ground, or both!
To be completely honest if you have the right mentallity you can play this game and beat it ( and then go get DLC and beat it some more ) in a few months (yes months you speed players MONTHS)

Don't let the negative reviews fool you. Yes it isn't Metal Slug, but just because it looks like it, it shouldnt play like it. This a Metal Slug style with a Monster Hunter vibe to it. The ability to customize your gun into any shape or form is the drive to this game. Now unless you wanna unlock every gun part, yes it WILL be a grind, but if you know what you want, you'll blaze through this game. By want I mean, you know what kind of gun you'll want to make. Spread patterns are all the same (this aint Counter Strike son), so a gun with 90% Acc will be the same across all fields, is just the ammunition that affects the pattern (Buckshots will not follow the same predetermined path as a Magnum Bullet). The only downfall this game has is there is no seamless map, you'll have to do different missions to go to the different maps. You will be doing the same maps over and over a couple of times, but you will be doing different parts of it to complete objectives. This can be a good or bad thing, as the missions are planned out so you know where to go for the main boss of the area (As bosses can/will run away to different parts of the map, and will need to know how to get there from previous playings). I find this game enjoyable, as others not so much, and for vain reasons.
PROS
-Customized Weapons
-Variety of Parts
-4 Player Co-Op (Both Online and Local)[Unknown if it can be mixed]
-Great Boss Battles
-Rainbow Dog of Doom that craps rockets at you
-Large Maps
-Shared Items in Co-Op mode (When finding, not crafting)
-Tougher Enemies in Co-Op mode
CONS
-Low Replayablity
-2 Characters
-Enemy Variety is low (In the beginning)
-Farm to Unlock all Parts
-Few Maps
-You will hate Rainbow Dog of Doom

Have you ever wished Hotline Miami was in the Old West, had a better sense of humor, and was hand-drawn black-and-white? Then you should get 12 is Better Than 6.
Although its gameplay is undeniably close to Hotline Miami's, 12 > 6 has a few unique facets that set it apart. First of all, there are several ways to manage weapons. You must right click to prepare several between shots, can manually reload them, and can empty them to store the ammo for later, even if you change weapons in the meantime.
Secondly, you have a few clumps of dynamite. Their blast radius is somewhat disappointing, but an AoE projectile is always nice to have.
Third, enemies have friendly fire, which is a welcome difference.
Finally, two of the most common cheese tactics no longer work. Guns are physical objects, so a character with their gun extended can't simply be sprinted up to and knifed; they must be strafed. Doors are also not impregnable heavyweight boxers, and may be fired through and deal no contact damage.
Overall, 12 is Better Than 6 is just a fun, fast-play top-down shooter, with the only arguable drawback of being perpetually stark white.
An excellent game all around and an example of how epic 2D Top Down Shooters can be.

A very fun and very accessible rogue-like, loaded with content and numerous class/race/item unlockables you earn just by playing.  Has a large number of races and classes that all feel different from one another, different difficulty settings (how many lives you get) and unlockable bonus campaigns (such as an endless dungeon and arena).  The game is free on their site, but buying or donating gets you a few extra perks, such as transferring items between characters, a dwarf-only class (Stone Warden) and an infinite lives mode.
The game doesn't hide anything from the player, so you'll know exactly what each stat point and skill does, what every piece of equipment will do for you, and exactly how strong each enemy is.  It's not gonna stop a wayward lightning bolt from ruining your run, though!
I already put dozens of hours into it before buying it, and have already put 2 dozen in since.  Wholeheartedly recommended!

A great Roguelike that makes it easy to get into the genre
Just like Dungeons of Dreadmore of SWOTS: The Pit, this game eases you into the idea of a Roguelike gently so that you can try it out without it being quite as brutal as, say, Nethack or DoomRL. The graphics are not a selling point in this title, but the gameplay should be. With tons of unlocks, lots of ways to stat and build characters, castes and quests to choose that will vary gameplay widely, and a big variety of enemies, if you've never gotten into a RL before but would like to try, get this.
If you're like me and more experienced in the genre, I still recommend it as this does some interesting things with the forumula--the capacity for kind of rogue-like not-quite-permadeath; the ability to (for example) forswear all arcane magic in exchange for joining a new faction of the game and learning magic-disrupting powers; the fact that one school of magic is powered mostly by paradox (and you can meet and kill yourself! ?.?) means that this is much more in-depth a game than the RLs of the 90s. Sure, you can pick this up free on the developer's website, but you should pay for it (here or there) just to support the effort.
8.5 out of 10--which back in the old days on PC Gamer, meant that this is a classic well worth your time. :)

A really impressive turn based roguelike with randomly generated quests, maps, and just about everything else. I have yet to dig more deeply into this game but I can tell its very good and has a whole lot of depth to it.

I've been playing this game in its various incarnations since it was PernAngband in the 1990s, then Troubles of MIddle Earth, and now finally Tales of Maj'Eyal - free from copyright infringement and better than ever!
It's truly exceptional, and these days, comes with so many lovely enhancements that Roguelikes have traditionally lacked. Mouse control, skill hotkeys, unlockables and stat tracking, and global chat with other playters, MMO-style, in the game window.
Underneath all this is a game system that is elegant, varied, and will keep you occupied for hours upon hours upon hours. Each character plays differently and has a host of interesting skill trees to work through. The dungeons are randomly generated, of course, but within some boundaries that ensure that each has its own flavour and unique style.
Death is permanent, as with all roguelikes (although there is another little helping hand in "Adventure" mode which gives you a few extra lives to play with) but whenever I lose a character it's never a crushing blow - because now I get to enjoy starting over with a brand new one.
You can download this game for free from
but it's well worth a fiver to support DarkGod and help him keep updating this brilliant title.
